items.title: PHP core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
items.excerpt: CVSSv3 Score: 9.8 CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).CVE-2026-109619PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. items.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching
items.excerpt: CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . These vulnerabilities, known as “php2shell,” allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP and affect all PHP installations serving web requests. Organizations should immediately update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 to fix these vulnerabilities. items.title: The new PHP flaw is separate from the two critical #PHP2Shell bugs patched on October 21. CVE-2026-115560 is NOT fixed by those emergency up
items.excerpt:
The new PHP flaw is separate from the two critical #PHP2Shell bugs patched on October 21.

CVE-2026-115560 is NOT fixed by those emergency updates.

PHP says exploitation requires an unusual session configuration and considers the risk unlikely in practice.

No attacks reported.

items.title: PHP has a one-line mitigation for CVE-2026-115560: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 This disables session upload progress until the fix arr
items.excerpt:
PHP has a one-line mitigation for CVE-2026-115560:

session.upload_progress.enabled=0

This disables session upload progress until the fix arrives in a routine release.

Already applied this mitigation for CVE-2026-109619? No further action is needed.

Why isn't PHP issuing another emergency patch?
